papers.title: Substitutions in woolly mammoth hemoglobin confer temperature-independent oxygen delivery

chunks.text: We investigated the molecular adaptations and genomic divergence of Mammuthus primigenius (Woolly Mammoth), an extinct taxon of the Late Pleistocene (300,000–4,000 BP). Targeting the HBB locus, paleogenomic sequencing revealed key adaptive substitutions distinguishing Mammuthus primigenius from extant sister species Elephas maximus (Asian Elephant). These mutations underlie cold-resistant oxygen delivery, providing molecular evidence for deep-time physiological adaptations to Quaternary environmental pressures.

Comparative alignment of Mammuthus primigenius and Elephas maximus HBB identified cataloged substitutions including T12A (Reduces oxygenation enthalpy for cold-adaptive oxygen delivery), A86S (Stabilizes T-state deoxy conformation in arctic cold), E101Q (Modulates allosteric chloride ion binding pocket). Structural homology modeling and crystallographic coordinates confirm that these derived amino acid substitutions alter local electrostatic surfaces and thermodynamic stability, directly conferring cold-resistant oxygen delivery.

Phylogenetic reconstruction confirms Adaptive paleogenomic amino acid substitutions in beta-globin reduce the temperature-dependence of oxygen affinity, allowing oxygen delivery to freezing peripheral limb tissues on the arctic steppe. The HBB substitutions in Mammuthus primigenius demonstrate that paleogenomic selection was concentrated on metabolic and structural pathways. The divergence between Mammuthus primigenius and Elephas maximus highlights the role of Pleistocene climatic oscillations in driving rapid molecular divergence.

papers.title: Complete genomes reveal signatures of demographic decline in woolly mammoths

chunks.text: In this paleogenomic survey of Mammuthus primigenius (Woolly Mammoth), we analyzed temporal population trajectories and genetic load preceding extinction (~4,000 BP (Wrangel Island)). High-coverage paleogenomic sequencing of Wrangel Island and Siberian mainland mammoths showing extensive loss of genetic diversity and fixed deleterious mutations prior to extinction.

Our genomic and fossil evidence across Beringian and global horizons indicates that Mammuthus primigenius maintained demographic stability across multiple interglacials before abrupt terminal population contraction. Genetic diversity metrics indicate inbreeding and mutational load accumulated rapidly as populations fragmented.
